classification.summary: The BPool credited swapExactAmountIn with the requested tokenAmountIn instead of the amount actually received, and exposed a permissionless gulp() that resyncs a token's recorded balance to the real one, so repeatedly swapping the 1%-transfer-fee token STA and calling gulp drove the pool's recorded STA balance to 1 wei and let 1 STA be swapped out for essentially the whole WETH side - the pool's own accounting, not any external price, is what failed.

sources.note: onchain review: BPool 0x0e511aa1a137aad267dfe3a6bfca0b856c1a3682 (STA/WETH) was created 2020-05-29T13:57:13Z at block 10160718 by 0x43189898d712df36d37c41d2897843482f729c65 through BFactory 0x9424b1412450d0f8fc2255faf6046b98213b76bd, unrelated to attack sender 0xbf675c80540111a310b06e1482f9127ef4e7469a or its attack contract 0x81d73c55458f024cdc82bbf27468a2deaa631407. A BPool is a plain non-proxy contract; its codehash is identical (0x974df1c33872ba8aab782be5117ff348802441590f84ed7701d734bb9c21683e) at the creation block and at the block before the incident, so the age is measured from deployment: 30.23 days. Classified code-bug rather than a mere token incompatibility because the defect is in the deployed pool code - it books tokenAmountIn rather than the delta actually received, and gulp() lets anyone rewrite the recorded balance. Loss not recorded in USD: the pool's WETH balance fell from 455.924127 to 0.077179 WETH inside the transaction (455.85 WETH taken). Order-of-magnitude sanity check only (ETH ~ $225 in June 2020, so ~$0.1m): far above the $1,000 floor. This row covers the STA pool only; a second Balancer pool (STONK) was drained the same day in a separate transaction.
loss converted at the incident timestamp (1593367391) via DefiLlama coins: 455.85 WETH x $226.73 = $103,353
